why: An endpoint change with the exact status, body, ordering of checks and side effects that must not happen, plus the three client surfaces affected. Larger than the others but still one behaviour.

task.summary: Make POST /signup reject a missing, empty or whitespace-only username with a 422 response and a machine-readable error, instead of creating an account with a blank username.

story.role: a support agent investigating accounts that cannot be found by name
story.benefit: no more accounts are created that nobody can search for or sign in to

impactedAreas.impact: Receives a new 422 error with code "username_required". It already shows the message field of 422 errors, so no change is needed, but the web team should confirm the wording.
Same new error. Versions before 4.2 show a generic failure for unknown error codes, which is acceptable.
Not changed by this task. Cleaning them up is separate work.

task.goal: Validate the username in the signup handler before any database write, and return a consistent error for blank values.

acceptance.behavior: A username that is missing, null, an empty string, or only whitespace is rejected with HTTP 422 and the JSON body {"error": {"code": "username_required", "message": "Enter a username."}}.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a signup request whose JSON body has username "   " and a valid email and password
When it is sent to POST /signup
Then the response status is 422
And the response body is {"error": {"code": "username_required", "message": "Enter a username."}}

acceptance.behavior: When the username is rejected, no row is inserted into the users table and no welcome email is queued.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a signup request with username ""
When it is sent to POST /signup
Then the users table has the same number of rows as before
And the email queue has no new job
acceptance.evidence: handler test with the test database and the in-memory queue

acceptance.behavior: A valid username is trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace and signup otherwise behaves exactly as it does today.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a signup request with username "  ada  " and a valid email and password
When it is sent to POST /signup
Then the response status is 201
And the created user's username is "ada"

acceptance.behavior: The username check runs before the existing email and password checks, so a request with a blank username and an invalid email reports only username_required.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a signup request with username "" and email "not-an-email"
When it is sent to POST /signup
Then the response status is 422
And the error code is "username_required"

testCases.description: POST /signup with username omitted, null, "", "   " and "\t\n" each returns 422 with exactly the username_required body.
After each rejected request in T-1, the users table row count is unchanged and the in-memory email queue is empty.
POST /signup with username "  ada  " returns 201 and stores "ada"; the existing happy-path signup test still passes unmodified.
POST /signup with username "" and email "not-an-email" returns 422 with code username_required, not the email error.
POST /signup with a non-string username, the number 5, returns 422 with code username_required.

scenarios.omitted: Hidden scenarios are not implemented yet.

nonGoals: Rules about which characters a username may contain, or its length
Fixing accounts already created with blank usernames
Changing the error format of other endpoints

concerns: Public endpoint behaviour changes for clients sending blank usernames

reuse: The validationError(code, message) helper in src/errors.js, which already produces the 422 error shape used by the email and password checks
task.approach: Add the check at the top of the handler, before the existing validation, using the existing validationError helper.
